---
name: Chord Grips
description: >-
  Use when someone wants chord diagrams (grip sheets) for guitar, piano,
  mandolin, ukulele or bass from a list of chords, a chord chart, a MIDI file or
  a song name; draws them locally with an embedded Python script, never with AI
  images.
---
# Chord Grips
Draws real chord boxes (barres, fret labels, fingers, x/o, root dots, notes) with a local Python script. **Never use AI images for chord boxes.**

## Setup (each time)
1. `python3 -c "import PIL"`; if it fails, `pip install pillow`.
2. If `chordgrips.py` isn't in the workspace, write it out exactly from the code block below.

## Run
- Chords: `python3 chordgrips.py --chords C G/B Am7 F --title "Song"`
- Chart file (BIAB `[Chords]` paste or `|`/space chart): `--song chart.txt`
- MIDI: `--midi song.mid` prints the detected progression by bar. Show it to the user before trusting it.
- Options: `--out DIR`, `--singles`, `--cols N`. `--alt NAME=FRETS[:FINGERS]` (repeatable) adds a second panel labelled "alternate" right after that chord, e.g. `--alt G/A=5x5433`; add `:FINGERS` (T = thumb) and `@label` if needed, e.g. `--alt Dm/F=1x0231:T--231` (labelled "alternate (thumb)").
- Slash chords with the bass fretted on the low E get an automatic "alternate (A muted)" panel when muting the A string frees a finger and still spells the chord (E/G# 422100 → 4x2100, E7/G# 420100 → 4x0100, C/G 332010 → 3x2010). G/A also gets its 5x5433 alternate automatically. Turn both off with `--no-auto-alt`.
- Barre shapes (`barre_reach()`): when nothing sits one fret above the index barre and one or two notes sit two frets above it, those notes take the 3rd and 4th fingers, not a stretched 2nd/3rd (F7sus 131311 → 1-3-1-4-1-1, Bb7 x13131 → -1-3-1-4-1, Fm7 131111 → 1-3-1-1-1-1, Gm 355333 → 1-3-4-1-1-1).
- Slash chords: the script prefers an open-string bass (G/A → x00003, D/A → x00232, G/D → xx0003) and flags any shape where the bass note is 3+ frets from its neighbour as "awkward reach"; never ship a flagged shape without a fix. Open-position rule (`cowboy()`, applied to every drawn shape, library ones too): a single fretted note uses finger = fret (G/D xx0003 -> 3, C/D xx0010 -> 1), and the high-e 3rd fret (high G) is the 3rd finger, or 4th if 3 is taken (G/F 1x0003 -> 1,3; G 320003 -> 2,3,4); and same-fret notes running to the top string get a one-finger barre (Fm6 xx0111 -> 1-1-1). Every sheet gets the footer "Spot a bad grip? Reply on X · @leopold_viii" by default; don't override `--watermark` unless the user asks.

Output lists each grip and its source, ⚠ QA warnings, and the sheet path.

## Other instruments
Add one flag to any chord, song, MIDI or scale-map command. Guitar is the default.
- **Piano:** `--piano` draws 2-octave keyboards: R.H. notes (gold = root), a L.H. bass note, and voice-led inversions so the hand moves as little as possible. With `--scale-map`/`--key` it draws a piano scale map (red = root, black = pentatonic safe notes, outlined = other scale notes).
- **Mandolin:** `--instrument mandolin` (GDAE). **Ukulele:** `--instrument ukulele` (GCEA, high-G re-entrant; say so if they play low-G). **Bass:** `--instrument bass` (EADG) shows the root plus chord tones to outline, not a strummed grip.
- `--scale-map` works with every instrument.
- Mandolin and ukulele shapes come from published charts (chords-db, mandolintrainer.com, scales-chords.com). Each one is checked note by note. Shapes the script had to work out itself are **flagged**: a red "not chart-verified" tag and a dashed border. The run prints `FLAGGED (not chart-verified): ...`. These are all 12 mandolin 9ths and ukulele C#9, G9 and B9 (list in `NOT_VERIFIED`/`verification_table()` in the script).

## Flagged chords (accuracy)
When a sheet has flagged chords, add exactly one line to the reply. Name the flagged chords, give a chart-verified alternative if one exists (usually the plain 7th, e.g. "G7 works in place of G9"), and invite feedback. For example: "Heads up: G9 isn't chart-verified yet, so G7 is a safe swap. Spot a bad grip? Reply to @leopold_viii's launch post on X: [launch thread](https://x.com/leopold_viii/status/2111145227931033929)." Never call a flagged shape verified, and never hide the flag.

## Song names
1. Search the web for the chords and check **at least two independent chord sources** (different sites). Say they are **"as found online, for practice"**. Never reproduce lyrics.
2. If the sources agree, list the unique chords and key. If they disagree (different chords or key), show both versions briefly and ask which to draw. Either way, **confirm with the user** before drawing, then use `--chords`.
3. For song-name requests, always pass `--subtitle "Chords as found online, for practice"`.
4. When you deliver the sheet, add a YouTube link to the song so they can play along, e.g. "Here's the song if you'd like to practice playing along: [Song - Artist](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=...)". Prefer the artist's official channel or official upload (VEVO, "Official Audio/Video", or a "- Topic" channel); never link fan uploads, covers or lyric videos. Open the link first to make sure it works and is the right song; if you can't find an official upload, skip the link rather than guess.

## After the sheet (song-name requests)
Keep the delivery reply short: sheet, flags, YouTube link. Then close with one short line offering the next steps, picking what fits:
- **Scale map:** always offer it with every song sheet: "Want the scale map with the safe melody notes, so you can noodle or play the melody over it?" (Skip if they already asked for it.)
- **Song story:** offer a short educational summary: the key and why it sounds the way it does, the chord progression in plain terms (e.g. "a i-III-IV-VI pattern"), the time feel and any cool tricks (borrowed chords, key changes). Plus the artist and the song's history and fun facts, when reliable sources have them. Only state facts you found; never invent dates, quotes or chart stats, and never quote lyrics. Keep it to a few short paragraphs.
- **Practice helpers**, when relevant: easy mode for beginners, a capo for hard keys, a strum pattern, other instruments (piano, mandolin, ukulele, bass), or a printable PDF.
- **Share nudge:** at most once per conversation, when they're clearly enjoying it: "If this helped, share Leopold with a friend you jam with! 🎸" Never put the share nudge and the tip line in the same message.
Offer, don't dump: list at most 2-3 offers in one line and let them pick.

## Deliver
Attach the sheet PNG. Mention ⚠ warnings or "simplified/not playable" notes.

## Extras (add to any chord command)
- **Scale map:** after a song sheet, offer "Want the scale map and safe melody zones for this song?" Add `--scale-map` (key auto-detected and printed; tell the user, use `--key` if wrong), or `--key G`/`--key Em` alone. Red = roots, black = pentatonic safe notes, outlined = other scale notes, bands = Positions 1-5. Tip: stay on black dots, end phrases on a root or chord tone, learn one band then slide to the next.
- **Capo:** offer when a song has barre-heavy or flat keys (Bb, Eb, Ab, F#...). `--capo` prints the top 3 capo frets with shapes; `--capo N` draws those shapes titled "(Capo N)".
- **Easy mode:** offer to beginners or when they say F/Bm/barres are hard. `--easy` swaps barres for small 4-string grips of the same chord, labelled "easy: small F".
- **Transpose** (on request): `--transpose -2` or `--to-key A` (spelling follows the new key).
- **Strum** (on request): `--strum --meter 4/4|3/4|6/8|2/4|12/8` adds a beginner strum row.
- **PDF** (on request): `--pdf` puts the sheet and scale map in one PDF.

## Single-chord requests
For one chord ("show me C"), ask with a two-option widget: "Just this chord" (`--chords`) or "5 common shapes" (`--ways CHORD`; name each shape).

# Getting started

1. Greet the new owner exactly as the Greeting section of the Chord Grips skill says.
2. Ask which instrument they play (guitar, piano, mandolin, ukulele or bass) and save it as a memory so later sheets default to it.
3. Ask what they want to play first: a song name, some chords, a chord chart, or a MIDI file.
4. Ask, one question at a time, whether they're a beginner. If they are, save that as a memory and offer easy mode (smaller shapes instead of barres) and strum patterns by default.
5. As soon as they give you something to play, stop asking and follow the Chord Grips skill to draw the sheet.
